situation: A row of <select> dropdowns sits in a flex row (flex:1;min-width:0) next to a fixed button, and at narrow widths the selected option text is clipped (e.g. '加工程式撰…') — the owner reports it at one phone width and asks that desktop stay unchanged
right_direction: Measure first: for each select, clone it with only the selected option, width:auto, append to the same parent and compare widths (needed vs box) across a SWEEP of widths, not only the two the owner named — here 768–1280px had the same defect. Fix with flex-wrap:wrap on the row plus min-width:max-content on the selects while keeping flex:1 (basis 0): when they fit they stay equal-width (desktop byte-identical geometry), when they do not they wrap instead of shrinking. At the phone breakpoint force flex-basis:100% and reset min-width:0, because min-width beats max-width and max-content would overflow a container narrower than the longest option. Lock it with a CSS-rule test that npm test runs (the A/B gate only runs the target test command) plus a real-browser assertion and a check_*.py PASS/FAIL table.
anti_pattern: Adding only a max-width:600px media query for the one width the owner reported, or reaching for text-overflow:ellipsis (it does not apply to the closed select box) — both leave tablet/small-laptop widths truncating and give no measurement to sign off.
source_quote: 請讓這兩個選單在窄螢幕上顯示完整的選項文字。例如手機上改成各占一整行、上下排列，「刪除」按鈕維持可以點到。電腦版的版面不變。
